failure_definition: Graft infection requiring explant and reconstruction
causal_mechanism: Bacterial colonization on the graft surface, facilitated by the presence of Gram-negative bacteria such as Bordetella holmesii and Salmonella, which disrupt bacterial cell membranes and DNA replication
current_device_behavior: The Rifampin-soaked Dacron vascular graft provides antimicrobial properties to prevent infection, but is still susceptible to colonization by certain bacteria
failure_point: The graft surface, where bacterial colonization occurs and leads to infection
blocking_constraint: The lack of a broad-spectrum antimicrobial coating on the graft surface, which allows certain bacteria to colonize and cause infection
